documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM
INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) achieved its highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT in the financial year 2025-26, representing 112% of installed capacity. The company reported a gross refining margin (GRM) of $9.2 per barrel for the full year and $13.75 per barrel for the fourth quarter. CPCL is executing major capital projects, including the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project and a retail outlet expansion, totaling INR 2,000 crores over the next two to three years. Management highlighted that while logistical constraints and crude price volatility present challenges, the company's leverage position remains comfortable with a gross debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported its financial and operational performance for the fourth quarter and full year of FY25 during the earnings conference call.

guidance.claim: The company does not expect any maintenance and inspection in the first six months of the year, but has a scheduled maintenance and inspection close to September or October.
guidance.quote: First, reply to you , in the first 6 months, we don't see any M&I. So it may not be there. But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.

guidance.claim: The company hopes to complete its ongoing debottlenecking study in the coming year, 2026-27.
guidance.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

guidance.claim: The company expects the normal maintenance capital expenditure for the next two years to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores.
guidance.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

demand_outlook.claim: The company feels it will be able to sustain its long-term average net GRM or cracks over a month-long period.
demand_outlook.quote: When I look for a month average kind of a period, I feel I'll be able to sustain the long-term averages.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that Motor Spirit (MS) in the southern market has a shortfall where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Southern market demand for Motor Spirit is projected to grow around 4% to 5% while High-Speed Diesel growth is forecast at 3%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company's capital expenditure for the current year was INR 856 crores compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has started execution of the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The company expects a lot of commissioning from its retail outlet project in the year 2026-27.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The company's LOBS project is valued at INR 1,600 crores and the retail outlet project is valued at INR 400 crores, which will be executed over two to three years.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

capex_expansion.claim: The company expects its normal annual maintenance capex to be around INR 500 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: Total capital expenditure spent for the financial year FY25 was Rs. 673 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has full custody of the 1,200 acres of land required for the new refinery project.
capex_expansion.quote: So, about 600 acres, which was already with CPCL and another 600 acres, which was acquired in the process, both is in our possession and the pre-project activities of boundary wall construction, and all those things are almost at a big stage.

margins_costs.claim: The company's gross refining margin for the financial year 2025-26 was $9.2 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The gross refining margin, GRM, for financial year 2025- '26 was $9.2 per barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: The company's gross refining margin for the fourth quarter was $13.75 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The company's niche products contribute around 15% of its margins.
margins_costs.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7%–8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins.

margins_costs.claim: The Gross Refining Margin for the full year FY25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: For the full year, inventory resulted in a loss of $0.06 per barrel, or Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: Fuel and loss for the year came down to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: The reported GRM for 9M 2024-25 was $3.40 per barrel.
Operating expenditure (net) was reported at Rs 945 crore for 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved its highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity, in the financial year 2025-26.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, representing 111% of installed capacity, in the fourth quarter.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved its highest ever annual production of 5.139 MMT for diesel and 1.318 MMT for petrol.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved its highest ever distillate yield of 79.1% during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: The company secured 55% to 60% of its crude through long-term agreements.
orders_capacity.quote: Due to our flexible crude-sourcing mechanism, we have strategically secured 55% to 60% through long-term agreements, the remaining on short-term basis from diverse sources, allowing us to enhance flexibility and capitalize on price economies irrespective of what situation we are in.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for the year, equivalent to 99.5% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: In the fourth quarter, crude throughput was 2.974 MMT, reaching 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The Manali Refinery has an installed capacity of 10.5 MMTPA.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.18 at a gross level compared to 0.39 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's gross borrowings are INR 1,900 crores, while net borrowings are INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: The company recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, bringing the total dividend for the year to INR 62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity ratio as of March 31, 2025, stood at 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: Total absolute debt stood at Rs. 3,100 crores and net worth was Rs. 7,939 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024. Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value for the current year.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

risks_headwinds.claim: Logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility present challenges for the company.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company experienced a foreign exchange loss of approximately INR 200 crores for the quarter and around INR 350 crores for the full year.
risks_headwinds.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company experienced a short-term disturbance of 30% to 40% in its long-term agreements due to geopolitical issues.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management stated that uncertainties arising from the volatility of crude prices continue to pose a challenge.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: CST Under recovery for 9M 2024-25 was Rs 246 crore.
Exchange variation loss for 9M 2024-25 was Rs 122 crore.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects to see a lot of commissioning from its retail outlet project in the year 2026-27.
management_commitments.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects to execute its INR 2,000 crores of projects over the next two to three years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: The company hopes to complete its ongoing debottlenecking study in the coming year, 2026-27.
management_commitments.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that maintenance capital expenditure for each of the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores without the LOBS project, and about Rs. 700 to Rs. 800 crores per year with the LOBS project.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally. And with this project, another Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores you can add for each of the year. So, without this project, about Rs. 300 crores per year. With this project, about Rs. 700 to Rs. 800 crores per year.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that one of their crude units, Crude Unit 1 which caters to lubes, will go into maintenance around August or September 2025.
management_commitments.quote: In 2025, our refinery crude unit 1 which caters to lubes will go into maintenance around August, September.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
